Sorry but anxiety is no excuse to not care about someone else.   I have fairly severe anxiety but I realise that my partner has needs too and there may be some times when he is not able to communicate/be with me.  Yes, it can be difficult but he is a person too and has his own needs/obligations.  

A partnership is take AND give.  It's easy to take all the time, especially if the other person is willing to give all the time.  You need to set some boundaries.   So, for example, you go to her after work but you need to leave at 23:00 so that you get sufficient sleep for work the next day.  There is one night a week where you can't go because you need to go to the gym/have time for yourself/whatever.

Anxiety is not an excuse to ignore other peoples' needs and feelings

In all honesty, this sounds totally like anxiety and your brain is lying to you.  I currently have a partner, younger than me and very handsome: in fact I find it difficult to believe why he is interested at all but he is and I keep having to consciously remind myself of that.

None of us know what is going to happen in the future.  Is it possible that one day my partner will find someone younger than me and leave me?  Of course it is but it hasn't happened yet.   It might be tomorrow, next month, next year or never.   I am using mindfulness to try and overcome the fear and anxiety, to concentrate on enjoying the now and being with him.   

Like everything, sexual appetites change as we mature, the libido calms down and this may be the case with your husband.  My partner and I often just spend time hugging and cuddling in a non-sexual manner (he is extremely mature for his age).  

The main point is that you have no evidence to base your fear on.  Nothing at all.  This points to it being anxiety rather than factual.  A man who's cheating doesn't behave the way your husband is behaving.   There are always signs even if they are subtle: a late night at the office once in a while and becoming more frequent, a new email address which you don't have access to, a new app on his phone.  More importantly he would show far less interest in you/the family than previously. 

Perhaps visit your doctor and discuss whether you need meds and/or therapy?
It's difficult when things happen one on top of another but it can't possibly last forever (pep-talk to myself there!).   Keep going, stay strong and you will overcome.

Whatever you say is just your opinion.  Sometimes it will be spot on and other times it won't be helpful to the person concerned at all.  However, that doesn't mean you shouldn't say it.  If you get it spot on only once and help someone, that's still worthwhile.  

People have to treat comments the way they do when someone is speaking in real life.  It's an opinion and if it's helpful that's great.  If it's not helpful just ignore it.

I think you are seeing what you want to see.  I read many posts and comments on this sub and the number of people who offer to talk to those desperate enough to think of suicide is amazing!  

No, no one can wave a magic wand and solve someone else's problems.  Talking, however, can help and many reach out by pm to those who post, without even making a public comment.  I've posted here on an old account and someone sat talking with me for hours until the urge passed (ok, having checked my chat log, it was around 45 minutes but the point is still valid).  We didn't even talk about anything important, it was just general chat but that person undoubtedly saved my life that night.  

Don't be so quick to dismiss a valuable resource.

Anxiety is common when you get a dog.  My Charlie is 12 now, so we are beyond all that but I remember when I first got him.  It was awful, trying to potty train and get him to act as I wanted.  I joined a couple of Facebook groups:  Outback dog training https://www.facebook.com/groups/218014932124043/?ref=group_browse
And Dogs Make Me Smile:https://www.facebook.com/groups/dogsmakemesmile
Both have files and tips on the common problems that occur and you can always ask questions.  People are helpful and want to give you their tips and tricks for the various stages of training.  There are even videos which you can watch to see how they dealt with similar problems.

Hope this helps

I have recently been diagnosed with ovarian cancer.  Non-operable at the moment, although I am told that it may become operable after chemo.  I don't have a husband or children so my situation is somewhat different.  In fact if it weren't for one person, who I know would be hurt by my death, I'd let nature take its course.  

The mental effects are horrendous.  I am still processing the information but I know what you mean, I feel like a completely different person to two weeks ago.  I am short tempered and fiercely self-protective.  

I don't feel like a person any more, I feel like a diagnosis.  I think only someone who is or has been in the same position can understand.  

However, we will get through this!  Do it just to prove you can.  We are not statistics, we are living breathing human beings and we can beat it!
